name: Autosomal Dominant Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for HSAN Type I

criteria.description: Progressive distal sensory loss predominantly affecting pain and temperature modalities
Presence of autonomic disturbances including anhidrosis and orthostatic hypotension
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Electrophysiological evidence of sensory neuronopathy or axonal neuropathy
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes such as SPTLC1 or SPTLC2

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal sensory loss and autonomic dysfunction with a compatible autosomal dominant family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory but not mandatory if clinical criteria are met

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal loss of pain and temperature sensation
searchTerms: loss of pain and temperature feeling in feet
reduced sensation to heat and pain

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anhidrosis (absence of sweating) in affected regions
searchTerms: no sweating in affected skin areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent painless foot ulcers leading to osteomyelitis
pathognomonic.notes: Due to sensory loss and repeated trauma
searchTerms: painless foot ulcers causing bone infection
repeated foot sores leading to osteomyelitis
chronic foot wounds with bone infection
weakness and muscle loss in hands and feet
loss of strength in fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in lower limbs
Gait disturbance due to sensory ataxia
searchTerms: loss of balance due to sensory problems

laboratory: Elevated serum neurofilament light chain in some cases
imaging: MRI may show spinal cord atrophy in advanced cases
Bone X-rays demonstrating osteomyelitis or fractures secondary to neuropathy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SPTLC1, SPTLC2 genes
Other rare mutations in genes associated with HSAN Type I
other: Nerve biopsy showing loss of small myelinated and unmyelinated fibers

distinguishingFeatures: More severe sensory loss with ulcerations
Multisystem involvement including renal failure and cardiac disease

redFlags: Rapid progression of sensory loss with severe autonomic instability
Development of painless foot ulcers with osteomyelitis
Family history of similar neuropathy with dominant inheritance
references: Orphanet: Autosomal Dominant Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy (ORPHA:140474)
Dyck PJ, et al. Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies: clinical and genetic classification. Brain. 1993.
Rotthier A, et al. Genes and mechanisms in hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies. Nat Rev Neurol. 2012.
